t: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner -

r: The Criterion 25:2
t: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.

r: The Criterion 25:3
t: But they have taken besides Him gods which create nothing, while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit and possess not [power to cause] death or life or resurrection.

r: The Criterion 25:4
t: And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur’ān] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.

r: The Criterion 25:5
t: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."

r: The Criterion 25:6
t: Say, [O Muḥammad], "It has been revealed by He who knows [every] secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

r: The Criterion 25:7
t: And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him a warner?

r: The Criterion 25:8
t: Or [why is not] a treasure presented to him [from heaven], or does he [not] have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."

r: The Criterion 25:9
t: Look how they strike for you comparisons; but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.

r: The Criterion 25:10
t: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could have made for you [something] better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and could make for you palaces.

r: The Criterion 25:11
t: But they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.

r: The Criterion 25:12
t: When it [i.e., the Hellfire] sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring.

r: The Criterion 25:13
t: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein bound in chains, they will cry out thereupon for destruction.

r: The Criterion 25:14
t: [They will be told], "Do not cry this Day for one destruction but cry for much destruction."

r: The Criterion 25:15
t: Say, "Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination.

r: The Criterion 25:16
t: For them therein is whatever they wish, [while] abiding eternally. It is ever upon your Lord a promise [worthy to be] requested.

r: The Criterion 25:17
t: And [mention] the Day He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allāh and will say, "Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they [themselves] stray from the way?"

r: The Criterion 25:18
t: They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for us to take besides You any allies [i.e., protectors]. But You provided comforts for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined."

r: The Criterion 25:19
t: So they will deny you, [disbelievers], in what you say, and you cannot avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever commits injustice among you - We will make him taste a great punishment.

r: The Criterion 25:20
t: And We did not send before you, [O Muḥammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing.

r: The Criterion 25:21
t: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with great insolence.

r: The Criterion 25:22
t: The day they see the angels - no good tidings will there be that day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."

r: The Criterion 25:23
t: And We will approach [i.e., regard] what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed.

r: The Criterion 25:24
t: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are [in] a better settlement and better resting place.

r: The Criterion 25:25
t: And [mention] the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.

r: The Criterion 25:26
t: True sovereignty, that Day, is for the Most Merciful. And it will be upon the disbelievers a difficult Day.

r: The Criterion 25:27
t: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.

r: The Criterion 25:28
t: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one as a friend.

r: The Criterion 25:29
t: He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."

r: The Criterion 25:30
t: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’ān as [a thing] abandoned."

r: The Criterion 25:31
t: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.

r: The Criterion 25:32
t: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.

r: The Criterion 25:33
t: And they do not come to you with an example [i.e., argument] except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.

r: The Criterion 25:34
t: The ones who are gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in [their] way.

r: The Criterion 25:35
t: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.

r: The Criterion 25:36
t: And We said, "Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.

r: The Criterion 25:37
t: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.

r: The Criterion 25:38
t: And [We destroyed] ʿAad and Thamūd and the companions of the well and many generations between them.

r: The Criterion 25:39
t: And for each We presented examples [as warnings], and each We destroyed with [total] destruction.

r: The Criterion 25:40
t: And they have already come upon the town which was showered with a rain of evil [i.e., stones]. So have they not seen it? But they are not expecting resurrection.

r: The Criterion 25:41
t: And when they see you, [O Muḥammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one whom Allāh has sent as a messenger?

r: The Criterion 25:42
t: He almost would have misled us from our gods had we not been steadfast in [worship of] them." But they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is farthest astray in [his] way.

r: The Criterion 25:43
t: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?

r: The Criterion 25:44
t: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock. Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.

r: The Criterion 25:45
t: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.

r: The Criterion 25:46
t: Then We [retract and] hold it with Us for a brief grasp.

r: The Criterion 25:47
t: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection.

r: The Criterion 25:48
t: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy [i.e., rainfall], and We send down from the sky pure water

r: The Criterion 25:49
t: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men.

r: The Criterion 25:50
t: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded, but most of the people refuse except disbelief.

r: The Criterion 25:51
t: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.

r: The Criterion 25:52
t: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a great striving.

r: The Criterion 25:53
t: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas [i.e., bodies of water], one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.

r: The Criterion 25:54
t: And it is He who has created from water [i.e., semen] a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent [concerning creation].

r: The Criterion 25:55
t: But they worship rather than Allāh that which does not benefit them or harm them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].

r: The Criterion 25:56
t: And We have not sent you, [O Muḥammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.

r: The Criterion 25:57
t: Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way."

r: The Criterion 25:58
t: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allāh] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, [fully] Aware -

r: The Criterion 25:59
t: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)].

r: The Criterion 25:60
t: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" And it increases them in aversion.

r: The Criterion 25:61
t: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.

r: The Criterion 25:62
t: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.

r: The Criterion 25:63
t: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace,

r: The Criterion 25:64
t: And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer]

r: The Criterion 25:65
t: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering;

r: The Criterion 25:66
t: Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence."

r: The Criterion 25:67
t: And [they are] those who, when they spend, do so not excessively or sparingly but are ever, between that, [justly] moderate

r: The Criterion 25:68
t: And those who do not invoke with Allāh another deity or kill the soul which Allāh has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.

r: The Criterion 25:69
t: Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated -

r: The Criterion 25:70
t: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allāh will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.

r: The Criterion 25:71
t: And he who repents and does righteousness does indeed turn to Allāh with [accepted] repentance.

r: The Criterion 25:72
t: And [they are] those who do not testify to falsehood, and when they pass near ill speech, they pass by with dignity.

r: The Criterion 25:73
t: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.

r: The Criterion 25:74
t: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."

r: The Criterion 25:75
t: Those will be awarded the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace,

r: The Criterion 25:76
t: Abiding eternally therein. Good is the settlement and residence.

r: The Criterion 25:77
t: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?" For you [disbelievers] have denied, so it [i.e., your denial] is going to be adherent.

r: The Poets 26:1
t: Ṭā, Seen, Meem.

r: The Poets 26:2
t: These are the verses of the clear Book.

r: The Poets 26:3
t: Perhaps, [O Muḥammad], you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers.

r: The Poets 26:4
t: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.

r: The Poets 26:5
t: And no mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it.

r: The Poets 26:6
t: For they have already denied, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to ridicule.

r: The Poets 26:7
t: Did they not look at the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind?

r: The Poets 26:8
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:9
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:10
t: And [mention] when your Lord called Moses, [saying], "Go to the wrongdoing people -

r: The Poets 26:11
t: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear Allāh?"

r: The Poets 26:12
t: He said, "My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me

r: The Poets 26:13
t: And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent, so send for Aaron.

r: The Poets 26:14
t: And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."

r: The Poets 26:15
t: [Allāh] said, "No. Go both of you with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.

r: The Poets 26:16
t: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds,

r: The Poets 26:17
t: [Commanded to say], "Send with us the Children of Israel."'"

r: The Poets 26:18
t: [Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?

r: The Poets 26:19
t: And [then] you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful."

r: The Poets 26:20
t: [Moses] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray [i.e., ignorant].

r: The Poets 26:21
t: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement [i.e., wisdom and prophet hood] and appointed me [as one] of the messengers.

r: The Poets 26:22
t: And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?"

r: The Poets 26:23
t: Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"

r: The Poets 26:24
t: [Moses] said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced."

r: The Poets 26:25
t: [Pharaoh] said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"

r: The Poets 26:26
t: [Moses] said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers."

r: The Poets 26:27
t: [Pharaoh] said, "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."

r: The Poets 26:28
t: [Moses] said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason."

r: The Poets 26:29
t: [Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."

r: The Poets 26:30
t: [Moses] said, "Even if I brought you something [i.e., proof] manifest?"

r: The Poets 26:31
t: [Pharaoh] said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful."

r: The Poets 26:32
t: So [Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.

r: The Poets 26:33
t: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers.

r: The Poets 26:34
t: [Pharaoh] said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician.

r: The Poets 26:35
t: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?"

r: The Poets 26:36
t: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers

r: The Poets 26:37
t: Who will bring you every learned, skilled magician."

r: The Poets 26:38
t: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.

r: The Poets 26:39
t: And it was said to the people, "Will you congregate.

r: The Poets 26:40
t: That we might follow the magicians if they are the predominant?"

r: The Poets 26:41
t: And when the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?"

r: The Poets 26:42
t: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be of those near [to me]."

r: The Poets 26:43
t: Moses said to them, "Throw whatever you will throw."

r: The Poets 26:44
t: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are predominant."

r: The Poets 26:45
t: Then Moses threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified.

r: The Poets 26:46
t: So the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allāh].

r: The Poets 26:47
t: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds,

r: The Poets 26:48
t: The Lord of Moses and Aaron."

r: The Poets 26:49
t: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Moses] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, but you are going to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."

r: The Poets 26:50
t: They said, "No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return.

r: The Poets 26:51
t: Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers."

r: The Poets 26:52
t: And We inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."

r: The Poets 26:53
t: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers

r: The Poets 26:54
t: [And said], "Indeed, those are but a small band,

r: The Poets 26:55
t: And indeed, they are enraging us,

r: The Poets 26:56
t: And indeed, we are a cautious society..."

r: The Poets 26:57
t: So We removed them from gardens and springs

r: The Poets 26:58
t: And treasures and honorable station -

r: The Poets 26:59
t: Thus. And We caused to inherit it the Children of Israel.

r: The Poets 26:60
t: So they pursued them at sunrise.

r: The Poets 26:61
t: And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken!"

r: The Poets 26:62
t: [Moses] said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."

r: The Poets 26:63
t: Then We inspired to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.

r: The Poets 26:64
t: And We advanced thereto the others [i.e., the pursuers].

r: The Poets 26:65
t: And We saved Moses and those with him, all together.

r: The Poets 26:66
t: Then We drowned the others.

r: The Poets 26:67
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:68
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:69
t: And recite to them the news of Abraham,

r: The Poets 26:70
t: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"

r: The Poets 26:71
t: They said, "We worship idols and remain to them devoted."

r: The Poets 26:72
t: He said, "Do they hear you when you supplicate?

r: The Poets 26:73
t: Or do they benefit you, or do they harm?"

r: The Poets 26:74
t: They said, "But we found our fathers doing thus."

r: The Poets 26:75
t: He said, "Then do you see what you have been worshipping,

r: The Poets 26:76
t: You and your ancient forefathers?

r: The Poets 26:77
t: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds,

r: The Poets 26:78
t: Who created me, and He [it is who] guides me.

r: The Poets 26:79
t: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink.

r: The Poets 26:80
t: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me

r: The Poets 26:81
t: And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life

r: The Poets 26:82
t: And who I aspire that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense."

r: The Poets 26:83
t: [And he said], "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous.

r: The Poets 26:84
t: And grant me a mention [i.e., reputation] of honor among later generations.

r: The Poets 26:85
t: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure.

r: The Poets 26:86
t: And forgive my father. Indeed, he has been of those astray.

r: The Poets 26:87
t: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are [all] resurrected -

r: The Poets 26:88
t: The Day when there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children

r: The Poets 26:89
t: But only one who comes to Allāh with a sound heart."

r: The Poets 26:90
t: And Paradise will be brought near [that Day] to the righteous.

r: The Poets 26:91
t: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators,

r: The Poets 26:92
t: And it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to worship

r: The Poets 26:93
t: Other than Allāh? Can they help you or help themselves?"

r: The Poets 26:94
t: So they will be overturned into it [i.e., Hellfire], they and the deviators

r: The Poets 26:95
t: And the soldiers of Iblees, all together.

r: The Poets 26:96
t: They will say while they dispute therein,

r: The Poets 26:97
t: "By Allāh, we were indeed in manifest error

r: The Poets 26:98
t: When we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:99
t: And no one misguided us except the criminals.

r: The Poets 26:100
t: So now we have no intercessors

r: The Poets 26:101
t: And not a devoted friend.

r: The Poets 26:102
t: Then if we only had a return [to the world] and could be of the believers..."

r: The Poets 26:103
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:104
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:105
t: The people of Noah denied the messengers

r: The Poets 26:106
t: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

r: The Poets 26:107
t: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

r: The Poets 26:108
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:109
t: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:110
t: So fear Allāh and obey me."

r: The Poets 26:111
t: They said, "Should we believe you while you are followed by the lowest [class of people]?"

r: The Poets 26:112
t: He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?

r: The Poets 26:113
t: Their account is only upon my Lord, if you [could] perceive.

r: The Poets 26:114
t: And I am not one to drive away the believers.

r: The Poets 26:115
t: I am only a clear warner."

r: The Poets 26:116
t: They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be of those who are stoned."

r: The Poets 26:117
t: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.

r: The Poets 26:118
t: Then judge between me and them with decisive judgement and save me and those with me of the believers."

r: The Poets 26:119
t: So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.

r: The Poets 26:120
t: Then We drowned thereafter the remaining ones.

r: The Poets 26:121
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:122
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:123
t: ʿAad denied the messengers

r: The Poets 26:124
t: When their brother Hūd said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

r: The Poets 26:125
t: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

r: The Poets 26:126
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:127
t: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:128
t: Do you construct on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves,

r: The Poets 26:129
t: And take for yourselves constructions [i.e., palaces and fortresses] that you might abide eternally?

r: The Poets 26:130
t: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.

r: The Poets 26:131
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:132
t: And fear He who provided you with that which you know,

r: The Poets 26:133
t: Provided you with grazing livestock and children

r: The Poets 26:134
t: And gardens and springs.

r: The Poets 26:135
t: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."

r: The Poets 26:136
t: They said, "It is all the same to us whether you advise or are not of the advisors.

r: The Poets 26:137
t: This is not but the custom of the former peoples,

r: The Poets 26:138
t: And we are not to be punished."

r: The Poets 26:139
t: And they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:140
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:141
t: Thamūd denied the messengers

r: The Poets 26:142
t: When their brother Ṣāliḥ said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

r: The Poets 26:143
t: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

r: The Poets 26:144
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:145
t: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:146
t: Will you be left in what is here, secure [from death],

r: The Poets 26:147
t: Within gardens and springs

r: The Poets 26:148
t: And fields of crops and palm trees with softened fruit?

r: The Poets 26:149
t: And you carve out of the mountains, homes, with skill.

r: The Poets 26:150
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:151
t: And do not obey the order of the transgressors,

r: The Poets 26:152
t: Who cause corruption in the land and do not amend."

r: The Poets 26:153
t: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.

r: The Poets 26:154
t: You are but a man like ourselves, so bring a sign, if you should be of the truthful."

r: The Poets 26:155
t: He said, "This is a she-camel. For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day.

r: The Poets 26:156
t: And do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by the punishment of a terrible day."

r: The Poets 26:157
t: But they hamstrung her and so became regretful.

r: The Poets 26:158
t: And the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:159
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:160
t: The people of Lot denied the messengers

r: The Poets 26:161
t: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

r: The Poets 26:162
t: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

r: The Poets 26:163
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:164
t: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:165
t: Do you approach males among the worlds

r: The Poets 26:166
t: And leave what your Lord has created for you as mates? But you are a people transgressing."

r: The Poets 26:167
t: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted."

r: The Poets 26:168
t: He said, "Indeed, I am, toward your deed, of those who detest [it].

r: The Poets 26:169
t: My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequence of] what they do."

r: The Poets 26:170
t: So We saved him and his family, all,

r: The Poets 26:171
t: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.

r: The Poets 26:172
t: Then We destroyed the others.

r: The Poets 26:173
t: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.

r: The Poets 26:174
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:175
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:176
t: The companions of the thicket [i.e., the people of Madyan] denied the messengers

r: The Poets 26:177
t: When Shuʿayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

r: The Poets 26:178
t: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

r: The Poets 26:179
t: So fear Allāh and obey me.

r: The Poets 26:180
t: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:181
t: Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss.

r: The Poets 26:182
t: And weigh with an even [i.e., honest] balance.

r: The Poets 26:183
t: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.

r: The Poets 26:184
t: And fear He who created you and the former creation."

r: The Poets 26:185
t: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.

r: The Poets 26:186
t: You are but a man like ourselves, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.

r: The Poets 26:187
t: So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you should be of the truthful."

r: The Poets 26:188
t: He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do."

r: The Poets 26:189
t: And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.

r: The Poets 26:190
t: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

r: The Poets 26:191
t: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Poets 26:192
t: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds.

r: The Poets 26:193
t: The Trustworthy Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] has brought it down

r: The Poets 26:194
t: Upon your heart, [O Muḥammad] - that you may be of the warners -

r: The Poets 26:195
t: In a clear Arabic language.

r: The Poets 26:196
t: And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples.

r: The Poets 26:197
t: And has it not been a sign to them that it is recognized by the scholars of the Children of Israel?

r: The Poets 26:198
t: And even if We had revealed it to one among the foreigners

r: The Poets 26:199
t: And he had recited it to them [perfectly], they would [still] not have been believers in it.

r: The Poets 26:200
t: Thus have We inserted it [i.e., disbelief] into the hearts of the criminals.

r: The Poets 26:201
t: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.

r: The Poets 26:202
t: And it will come to them suddenly while they perceive [it] not.

r: The Poets 26:203
t: And they will say, "May we be reprieved?"

r: The Poets 26:204
t: So for Our punishment are they impatient?

r: The Poets 26:205
t: Then have you considered if We gave them enjoyment for years

r: The Poets 26:206
t: And then there came to them that which they were promised?

r: The Poets 26:207
t: They would not be availed by the enjoyment with which they were provided.

r: The Poets 26:208
t: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners

r: The Poets 26:209
t: As a reminder; and never have We been unjust.

r: The Poets 26:210
t: And the devils have not brought it [i.e., the revelation] down.

r: The Poets 26:211
t: It is not allowable for them, nor would they be able.

r: The Poets 26:212
t: Indeed they, from [its] hearing, are removed.

r: The Poets 26:213
t: So do not invoke with Allāh another deity and [thus] be among the punished.

r: The Poets 26:214
t: And warn, [O Muḥammad], your closest kindred.

r: The Poets 26:215
t: And lower your wing [i.e., show kindness] to those who follow you of the believers.

r: The Poets 26:216
t: And if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you are doing."

r: The Poets 26:217
t: And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,

r: The Poets 26:218
t: Who sees you when you arise

r: The Poets 26:219
t: And your movement among those who prostrate.

r: The Poets 26:220
t: Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

r: The Poets 26:221
t: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?

r: The Poets 26:222
t: They descend upon every sinful liar.

r: The Poets 26:223
t: They pass on what is heard, and most of them are liars.

r: The Poets 26:224
t: And the poets - [only] the deviators follow them;

r: The Poets 26:225
t: Do you not see that in every valley they roam

r: The Poets 26:226
t: And that they say what they do not do? -

r: The Poets 26:227
t: Except those [poets] who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allāh often and defend [the Muslims] after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.

r: The Ant 27:1
t: Ṭā, Seen. These are the verses of the Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] and a clear Book

r: The Ant 27:2
t: As guidance and good tidings for the believers

r: The Ant 27:3
t: Who establish prayer and give zakāh, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].

r: The Ant 27:4
t: Indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made pleasing to them their deeds, so they wander blindly.

r: The Ant 27:5
t: Those are the ones for whom there will be the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers.

r: The Ant 27:6
t: And indeed, [O Muḥammad], you receive the Qur’ān from one Wise and Knowing.

r: The Ant 27:7
t: [Mention] when Moses said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves."

r: The Ant 27:8
t: But when he came to it, he was called, "Blessed is whoever is at the fire and whoever is around it. And exalted is Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

r: The Ant 27:9
t: O Moses, indeed it is I - Allāh, the Exalted in Might, the Wise."

r: The Ant 27:10
t: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allāh said], "O Moses, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear.

r: The Ant 27:11
t: Otherwise, he who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil - indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful.

r: The Ant 27:12
t: And put your hand into the opening of your garment [at the breast]; it will come out white without disease. [These are] among the nine signs [you will take] to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient."

r: The Ant 27:13
t: But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic."

r: The Ant 27:14
t: And they rejected them, while their [inner] selves were convinced thereof, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters.

r: The Ant 27:15
t: And We had certainly given to David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise [is due] to Allāh, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."

r: The Ant 27:16
t: And Solomon inherited David. He said, "O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty."

r: The Ant 27:17
t: And gathered for Solomon were his soldiers of the jinn and men and birds, and they were [marching] in rows

r: The Ant 27:18
t: Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Solomon and his soldiers while they perceive not."

r: The Ant 27:19
t: So [Solomon] smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants."

r: The Ant 27:20
t: And he took attendance of the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe - or is he among the absent?

r: The Ant 27:21
t: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me clear authorization."

r: The Ant 27:22
t: But he [i.e., the hoopoe] stayed not long and said, "I have encompassed [in knowledge] that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news.

r: The Ant 27:23
t: Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.

r: The Ant 27:24
t: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allāh, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from [His] way, so they are not guided,

r: The Ant 27:25
t: [And] so they do not prostrate to Allāh, who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare -

r: The Ant 27:26
t: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne."

r: The Ant 27:27
t: [Solomon] said, "We will see whether you were truthful or were of the liars.

r: The Ant 27:28
t: Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them. Then leave them and see what [answer] they will return."

r: The Ant 27:29
t: She said, "O eminent ones, indeed, to me has been delivered a noble letter.

r: The Ant 27:30
t: Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it is [i.e., reads]: 'In the name of Allāh, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,

r: The Ant 27:31
t: Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission [as Muslims].'"

r: The Ant 27:32
t: She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me."

r: The Ant 27:33
t: They said, "We are men of strength and of great military might, but the command is yours, so see what you will command."

r: The Ant 27:34
t: She said, "Indeed kings - when they enter a city, they ruin it and render the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do.

r: The Ant 27:35
t: But indeed, I will send to them a gift and see with what [reply] the messengers will return."

r: The Ant 27:36
t: So when they came to Solomon, he said, "Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allāh has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.

r: The Ant 27:37
t: Return to them, for we will surely come to them with soldiers that they will be powerless to encounter, and we will surely expel them therefrom in humiliation, and they will be debased."

r: The Ant 27:38
t: [Solomon] said, "O assembly [of jinn], which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"

r: The Ant 27:39
t: A powerful one from among the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [task] strong and trustworthy."

r: The Ant 27:40
t: Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."

r: The Ant 27:41
t: He said, "Disguise for her her throne; we will see whether she will be guided [to truth] or will be of those who is not guided."

r: The Ant 27:42
t: So when she arrived, it was said [to her], "Is your throne like this?" She said, "[It is] as though it was it." [Solomon said], "And we were given knowledge before her, and we have been Muslims [in submission to Allāh].

r: The Ant 27:43
t: And that which she was worshipping other than Allāh had averted her [from submission to Him]. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people."

r: The Ant 27:44
t: She was told, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins [to wade through]. He said, "Indeed, it is a palace [whose floor is] made smooth with glass." She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allāh, Lord of the worlds."

r: The Ant 27:45
t: And We had certainly sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ, [saying], "Worship Allāh," and at once they were two parties conflicting.

r: The Ant 27:46
t: He said, "O my people, why are you impatient for evil before [i.e., instead of] good? Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allāh that you may receive mercy?"

r: The Ant 27:47
t: They said, "We consider you a bad omen, you and those with you." He said, "Your omen [i.e., fate] is with Allāh. Rather, you are a people being tested."

r: The Ant 27:48
t: And there were in the city nine family heads causing corruption in the land and not amending [its affairs].

r: The Ant 27:49
t: They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allāh that we will kill him by night, he and his family. Then we will say to his executor, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'"

r: The Ant 27:50
t: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not.

r: The Ant 27:51
t: Then look how was the outcome of their plan - that We destroyed them and their people, all.

r: The Ant 27:52
t: So those are their houses, desolate because of the wrong they had done. Indeed in that is a sign for people who know.

r: The Ant 27:53
t: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allāh.

r: The Ant 27:54
t: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality while you are seeing?

r: The Ant 27:55
t: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly."

r: The Ant 27:56
t: But the answer of his people was not except that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."

r: The Ant 27:57
t: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind.

r: The Ant 27:58
t: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.

r: The Ant 27:59
t: Say, [O Muḥammad], "Praise be to Allāh, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allāh better or what they associate with Him?"

r: The Ant 27:60
t: [More precisely], is He [not best] who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not [otherwise] have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with Allāh? [No], but they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him].

r: The Ant 27:61
t: Is He [not best] who made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allāh? [No], but most of them do not know.

r: The Ant 27:62
t: Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth? Is there a deity with Allāh? Little do you remember.

r: The Ant 27:63
t: Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with Allāh? High is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

r: The Ant 27:64
t: Is He [not best] who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with Allāh? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

r: The Ant 27:65
t: Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allāh, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."

r: The Ant 27:66
t: Rather, their knowledge is arrested concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are, concerning it, blind.

r: The Ant 27:67
t: And those who disbelieve say, "When we have become dust as well as our forefathers, will we indeed be brought out [of the graves]?

r: The Ant 27:68
t: We have been promised this, we and our forefathers, before. This is not but legends of the former peoples."

r: The Ant 27:69
t: Say, [O Muḥammad], "Proceed [i.e., travel] through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals."

r: The Ant 27:70
t: And grieve not over them or be in distress from what they conspire.

r: The Ant 27:71
t: And they say, "When is [the fulfillment of] this promise, if you should be truthful?"

r: The Ant 27:72
t: Say, "Perhaps it is close behind you [i.e., very near] - some of that for which you are impatient.

r: The Ant 27:73
t: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of bounty for the people, but most of them are not grateful."

r: The Ant 27:74
t: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.

r: The Ant 27:75
t: And there is nothing concealed within the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear Register.

r: The Ant 27:76
t: Indeed, this Qur’ān relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they disagree.

r: The Ant 27:77
t: And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers.

r: The Ant 27:78
t: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His [wise] judgement. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

r: The Ant 27:79
t: So rely upon Allāh; indeed, you are upon the clear truth.

r: The Ant 27:80
t: Indeed, you will not make the dead hear, nor will you make the deaf hear the call when they have turned their backs retreating.

r: The Ant 27:81
t: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You will only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims [i.e., submitting to Allāh].

r: The Ant 27:82
t: And when the word [i.e., decree] befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith].

r: The Ant 27:83
t: And [warn of] the Day when We will gather from every nation a company of those who deny Our signs, and they will be [driven] in rows

r: The Ant 27:84
t: Until, when they arrive [at the place of Judgement], He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what [was it that] you were doing?"

r: The Ant 27:85
t: And the decree will befall them for the wrong they did, and they will not [be able to] speak.

r: The Ant 27:86
t: Do they not see that We made the night that they may rest therein and the day giving sight? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.

r: The Ant 27:87
t: And [warn of] the Day the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allāh wills. And all will come to Him humbled.

r: The Ant 27:88
t: And you see the mountains, thinking them motionless, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allāh, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Aware of that which you do.

r: The Ant 27:89
t: Whoever comes [at Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe.

r: The Ant 27:90
t: And whoever comes with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire, [and it will be said], "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"

r: The Ant 27:91
t: [Say, O Muḥammad], "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who made it sacred and to whom [belongs] all things. And I am commanded to be of the Muslims [i.e., those who submit to Allāh].

r: The Ant 27:92
t: And to recite the Qur’ān." And whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself; and whoever strays - say, "I am only [one] of the warners."

r: The Ant 27:93
t: And say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allāh. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do."

r: The Story 28:1
t: Ṭā, Seen, Meem.

r: The Story 28:2
t: These are verses of the clear Book.

r: The Story 28:3
t: We recite to you from the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe.

r: The Story 28:4
t: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their [newborn] sons and keeping their females alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters.

r: The Story 28:5
t: And We wanted to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors

r: The Story 28:6
t: And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and [his minister] Hāmān and their soldiers through them that which they had feared.

r: The Story 28:7
t: And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers."

r: The Story 28:8
t: And the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Hāmān and their soldiers were deliberate sinners.

r: The Story 28:9
t: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "[He will be] a comfort of the eye [i.e., pleasure] for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not.

r: The Story 28:10
t: And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of all else]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound fast her heart that she would be of the believers.

r: The Story 28:11
t: And she said to his sister, "Follow him"; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not.

r: The Story 28:12
t: And We had prevented from him [all] wet nurses before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere?"

r: The Story 28:13
t: So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allāh is true. But most of them [i.e., the people] do not know.

r: The Story 28:14
t: And when he attained his full strength and was [mentally] mature, We bestowed upon him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.

r: The Story 28:15
t: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy."

r: The Story 28:16
t: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

r: The Story 28:17
t: He said, "My Lord, for the favor You bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals."

r: The Story 28:18
t: And he became inside the city fearful and anticipating [exposure], when suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him [once again]. Moses said to him, "Indeed, you are an evident, [persistent] deviator."

r: The Story 28:19
t: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders."

r: The Story 28:20
t: And a man came from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, "O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conferring over you [intending] to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."

r: The Story 28:21
t: So he left it, fearful and anticipating [apprehension]. He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people."

r: The Story 28:22
t: And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way."

r: The Story 28:23
t: And when he came to the water [i.e., well] of Madyan, he found there a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women holding back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man."

r: The Story 28:24
t: So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need."

r: The Story 28:25
t: Then one of the two women came to him walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."

r: The Story 28:26
t: One of the women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."

r: The Story 28:27
t: He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allāh wills, from among the righteous."

r: The Story 28:28
t: [Moses] said, "That is [established] between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I complete - there is no injustice to me, and Allāh, over what we say, is Witness."

r: The Story 28:29
t: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there [some] information or burning wood from the fire that you may warm yourselves."

r: The Story 28:30
t: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree, "O Moses, indeed I am Allāh, Lord of the worlds."

r: The Story 28:31
t: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it was a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allāh said], "O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.

r: The Story 28:32
t: Insert your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out white, without disease. And draw in your arm close to you [as prevention] from fear, for those are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient."

r: The Story 28:33
t: He said, "My Lord, indeed I killed from among them someone, and I fear they will kill me.

r: The Story 28:34
t: And my brother Aaron is more fluent than me in tongue, so send him with me as support, verifying me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me."

r: The Story 28:35
t: [Allāh] said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both supremacy so they will not reach you. [It will be] through Our signs; you and those who follow you will be the predominant."

r: The Story 28:36
t: But when Moses came to them with Our signs as clear evidences, they said, "This is not except invented magic, and we have not heard of this [religion] among our forefathers."

r: The Story 28:37
t: And Moses said, "My Lord is more knowing [than we or you] of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be succession in the home. Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed."

r: The Story 28:38
t: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Hāmān, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars."

r: The Story 28:39
t: And he was arrogant, he and his soldiers, in the land, without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.

r: The Story 28:40
t: So We took him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.

r: The Story 28:41
t: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.

r: The Story 28:42
t: And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.

r: The Story 28:43
t: And We gave Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.

r: The Story 28:44
t: And you, [O Muḥammad], were not on the western side [of the mount] when We revealed to Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses [to that].

r: The Story 28:45
t: But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders [of this message].

r: The Story 28:46
t: And you were not at the side of the mount when We called [Moses] but [were sent] as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might be reminded.

r: The Story 28:47
t: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands put forth [of sins] and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?"...

r: The Story 28:48
t: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like that which was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They said, "[They are but] two works of magic supporting each other, and indeed we are, in both, disbelievers."

r: The Story 28:49
t: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allāh which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful."

r: The Story 28:50
t: But if they do not respond to you - then know that they only follow their [own] desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allāh? Indeed, Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

r: The Story 28:51
t: And We have [repeatedly] conveyed to them the word [i.e., the Qur’ān] that they might be reminded.

r: The Story 28:52
t: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they are believers in it.

r: The Story 28:53
t: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were, [even] before it, Muslims [i.e., submitting to Allāh]."

r: The Story 28:54
t: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and [because] they avert evil through good, and from what We have provided them they spend.

r: The Story 28:55
t: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you; we seek not the ignorant."

r: The Story 28:56
t: Indeed, [O Muḥammad], you do not guide whom you like, but Allāh guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.

r: The Story 28:57
t: And they [i.e., the Quraysh] say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.

r: The Story 28:58
t: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors.

r: The Story 28:59
t: And never would your Lord have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother [i.e., principal city] a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.

r: The Story 28:60
t: And whatever thing you [people] have been given - it is [only for] the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allāh is better and more lasting; so will you not use reason?

r: The Story 28:61
t: Then is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will meet [i.e., obtain] like he for whom We provided enjoyment of worldly life [but] then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment in Hell]?

r: The Story 28:62
t: And [warn of] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?"

r: The Story 28:63
t: Those upon whom the word will have come into effect will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation [from them] to You. They did not used to worship [i.e., obey] us."

r: The Story 28:64
t: And it will be said, "Invoke your 'partners,'" and they will invoke them; but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had followed guidance!

r: The Story 28:65
t: And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, "What did you answer the messengers?"

r: The Story 28:66
t: But the information will be unapparent to them that Day, so they will not [be able to] ask one another.

r: The Story 28:67
t: But as for one who had repented, believed, and done righteousness, it is expected [i.e., promised by Allāh] that he will be among the successful.

r: The Story 28:68
t: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allāh and high above what they associate with Him.

r: The Story 28:69
t: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.

r: The Story 28:70
t: And He is Allāh; there is no deity except Him. To Him is [due all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned.

r: The Story 28:71
t: Say, "Have you considered: if Allāh should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allāh could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"

r: The Story 28:72
t: Say, "Have you considered: if Allāh should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allāh could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"

r: The Story 28:73
t: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and [by day] seek from His bounty and [that] perhaps you will be grateful.

r: The Story 28:74
t: And [warn of] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?"

r: The Story 28:75
t: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof," and they will know that the truth belongs to Allāh, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.

r: The Story 28:76
t: Indeed, Qārūn was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allāh does not like the exultant.

r: The Story 28:77
t: But seek, through that which Allāh has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allāh has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allāh does not like corrupters."

r: The Story 28:78
t: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allāh had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.

r: The Story 28:79
t: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qārūn. Indeed, he is one of great fortune."

r: The Story 28:80
t: But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allāh is better for he who believes and does righteousness. And none are granted it except the patient."

r: The Story 28:81
t: And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allāh, nor was he of those who [could] defend themselves.

r: The Story 28:82
t: And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, "Oh, how Allāh extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it! If not that Allāh had conferred favor on us, He would have caused it to swallow us. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed!"

r: The Story 28:83
t: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.

r: The Story 28:84
t: Whoever comes [on the Day of Judgement] with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [as much as] what they used to do.

r: The Story 28:85
t: Indeed, [O Muḥammad], He who imposed upon you the Qur’ān will take you back to a place of return. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error."

r: The Story 28:86
t: And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.

r: The Story 28:87
t: And never let them avert you from the verses of Allāh after they have been revealed to you. And invite [people] to your Lord. And never be of those who associate others with Allāh.

r: The Story 28:88
t: And do not invoke with Allāh another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

r: The Spider 29:1
t: Alif, Lām, Meem.

r: The Spider 29:2
t: Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried?

r: The Spider 29:3
t: But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allāh will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.

r: The Spider 29:4
t: Or do those who do evil deeds think they can outrun [i.e., escape] Us? Evil is what they judge.

r: The Spider 29:5
t: Whoever should hope for the meeting with Allāh - indeed, the term [decreed by] Allāh is coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

r: The Spider 29:6
t: And whoever strives only strives for [the benefit of] himself. Indeed, Allāh is Free from need of the worlds.

r: The Spider 29:7
t: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.

r: The Spider 29:8
t: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.

r: The Spider 29:9
t: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous [into Paradise].

r: The Spider 29:10
t: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allāh," but when one [of them] is harmed for [the cause of] Allāh, he considers the trial [i.e., harm] of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allāh. But if victory comes from your Lord, they say, "Indeed, We were with you." Is not Allāh most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds [i.e., all creatures]?

r: The Spider 29:11
t: And Allāh will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.

r: The Spider 29:12
t: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.

r: The Spider 29:13
t: But they will surely carry their [own] burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.

r: The Spider 29:14
t: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.

r: The Spider 29:15
t: But We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.

r: The Spider 29:16
t: And [We sent] Abraham, when he said to his people, "Worship Allāh and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know.

r: The Spider 29:17
t: You only worship, besides Allāh, idols, and you produce a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allāh do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allāh provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned."

r: The Spider 29:18
t: And if you [people] deny [the message] - already nations before you have denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except [the duty of] clear notification.

r: The Spider 29:19
t: Have they not considered how Allāh begins creation and then repeats it? Indeed that, for Allāh, is easy.

r: The Spider 29:20
t: Say, [O Muḥammad], "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allāh will produce the final creation [i.e., development]. Indeed Allāh, over all things, is competent."

r: The Spider 29:21
t: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.

r: The Spider 29:22
t: And you will not cause failure [to Allāh] upon the earth or in the heaven. And you have not other than Allāh any protector or any helper.

r: The Spider 29:23
t: And the ones who disbelieve in the signs of Allāh and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment.

r: The Spider 29:24
t: And the answer of his [i.e., Abraham's] people was not but that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allāh saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.

r: The Spider 29:25
t: And [Abraham] said, "You have only taken, other than Allāh, idols as [a bond of] affection among you in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers."

r: The Spider 29:26
t: And Lot believed him. [Abraham] said, "Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."

r: The Spider 29:27
t: And We gave to him Isaac and Jacob and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture. And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.

r: The Spider 29:28
t: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.

r: The Spider 29:29
t: Indeed, you approach men and obstruct the road and commit in your meetings [every] evil." And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allāh, if you should be of the truthful."

r: The Spider 29:30
t: He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people."

r: The Spider 29:31
t: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that [i.e., Lot's] city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."

r: The Spider 29:32
t: [Abraham] said, "Indeed, within it is Lot." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife. She is to be of those who remain behind."

r: The Spider 29:33
t: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.

r: The Spider 29:34
t: Indeed, we will bring down on the people of this city punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient."

r: The Spider 29:35
t: And We have certainly left of it a sign as clear evidence for a people who use reason.

r: The Spider 29:36
t: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shuʿayb, and he said, "O my people, worship Allāh and expect the Last Day and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."

r: The Spider 29:37
t: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.

r: The Spider 29:38
t: And [We destroyed] ʿAad and Thamūd, and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. And Satan had made pleasing to them their deeds and averted them from the path, and they were endowed with perception.

r: The Spider 29:39
t: And [We destroyed] Qārūn and Pharaoh and Hāmān. And Moses had already come to them with clear evidences, and they were arrogant in the land, but they were not outrunners [of Our punishment].

r: The Spider 29:40
t: So each We seized for his sin; and among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the blast [from the sky], and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allāh would not have wronged them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.

r: The Spider 29:41
t: The example of those who take allies other than Allāh is like that of the spider who takes [i.e., constructs] a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if they only knew.

r: The Spider 29:42
t: Indeed, Allāh knows whatever thing they call upon other than Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

r: The Spider 29:43
t: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.

r: The Spider 29:44
t: Allāh created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.

r: The Spider 29:45
t: Recite, [O Muḥammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allāh is greater. And Allāh knows that which you do.

r: The Spider 29:46
t: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."

r: The Spider 29:47
t: And thus We have sent down to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān]. And those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture believe in it. And among these [people of Makkah] are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.

r: The Spider 29:48
t: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Then [i.e., otherwise] the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.

r: The Spider 29:49
t: Rather, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is distinct verses [preserved] within the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.

r: The Spider 29:50
t: But they say, "Why are not signs sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allāh, and I am only a clear warner."

r: The Spider 29:51
t: And is it not sufficient for them that We revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe.

r: The Spider 29:52
t: Say, "Sufficient is Allāh between me and you as Witness. He knows what is in the heavens and earth. And they who have believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allāh - it is those who are the losers."

r: The Spider 29:53
t: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. And if not for [the decree of] a specified term, punishment would have reached them. But it will surely come to them suddenly while they perceive not.

r: The Spider 29:54
t: They urge you to hasten the punishment. And indeed, Hell will be encompassing of the disbelievers

r: The Spider 29:55
t: On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from below their feet and it is said, "Taste [the result of] what you used to do."

r: The Spider 29:56
t: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.

r: The Spider 29:57
t: Every soul will taste death. Then to Us will you be returned.

r: The Spider 29:58
t: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely assign to them of Paradise [elevated] chambers beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers

r: The Spider 29:59
t: Who have been patient and upon their Lord rely.

r: The Spider 29:60
t: And how many a creature carries not its [own] provision. Allāh provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.

r: The Spider 29:61
t: If you asked them, "Who created the heavens and earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allāh." Then how are they deluded?

r: The Spider 29:62
t: Allāh extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts for him. Indeed Allāh is, of all things, Knowing.

r: The Spider 29:63
t: And if you asked them, "Who sends down rain from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" they would surely say, "Allāh." Say, "Praise to Allāh"; but most of them do not reason.

r: The Spider 29:64
t: And this worldly life is not but diversion and amusement. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the [eternal] life, if only they knew.

r: The Spider 29:65
t: And when they board a ship, they supplicate Allāh, sincere to Him in religion [i.e., faith and hope]. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him

r: The Spider 29:66
t: So that they will deny what We have granted them, and they will enjoy themselves. But they are going to know.

r: The Spider 29:67
t: Have they not seen that We made [Makkah] a safe sanctuary, while people are being taken away all around them? Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the favor of Allāh they disbelieve?

r: The Spider 29:68
t: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allāh or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a [sufficient] residence for the disbelievers?

r: The Spider 29:69
t: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allāh is with the doers of good.

r: The Romans 30:1
t: Alif, Lām, Meem.

r: The Romans 30:2
t: The Byzantines have been defeated

r: The Romans 30:3
t: In the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome

r: The Romans 30:4
t: Within three to nine years. To Allāh belongs the command [i.e., decree] before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice

r: The Romans 30:5
t: In the victory of Allāh. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

r: The Romans 30:6
t: [It is] the promise of Allāh. Allāh does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.

r: The Romans 30:7
t: They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware.

r: The Romans 30:8
t: Do they not contemplate within themselves? Allāh has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.

r: The Romans 30:9
t: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they plowed [or excavated] the earth and built it up more than they [i.e., the Makkans] have built it up, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allāh would not ever have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.

r: The Romans 30:10
t: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of Allāh and used to ridicule them.

r: The Romans 30:11
t: Allāh begins creation; then He will repeat it; then to Him you will be returned.

r: The Romans 30:12
t: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair.

r: The Romans 30:13
t: And there will not be for them among their [alleged] partners any intercessors, and they will [then] be disbelievers in their partners.

r: The Romans 30:14
t: And the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will become separated.

r: The Romans 30:15
t: And as for those who had believed and done righteous deeds, they will be in a garden [of Paradise], delighted.

r: The Romans 30:16
t: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the punishment [to remain].

r: The Romans 30:17
t: So exalted is Allāh when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.

r: The Romans 30:18
t: And to Him is [due all] praise throughout the heavens and the earth. And [exalted is He] at night and when you are at noon.

r: The Romans 30:19
t: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought out.

r: The Romans 30:20
t: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].
